30|c27c|  md("""ramabana is the *brain* of a coding agent, and nothing else. It has no editor, no
31|78e4|  frontend and no opinion about where it is running: everything it needs from the
32|7e70|  application around it arrives through one protocol, `Host`, and everything it needs
33|d81b|  from a model arrives through [rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi).
34|3def|  
35|622c|  It grew up inside [leela](https://github.com/vedicreader/leela), where it was already
36|5899|  written to this seam -- nothing in it ever imported the IDE -- and now stands on its own,
37|0fab|  with leela as its first consumer. It also ships its own two frontends, because a brain
38|f06e|  nobody can talk to is hard to judge: a terminal app and an MCP server, both built on the
39|721f|  same `Host`.""")

30|c27c|  md("""ramabana is the *brain* of a coding agent, and nothing else. It has no editor, no
31|78e4|  frontend and no opinion about where it is running: everything it needs from the
32|7e70|  application around it arrives through one protocol, `Host`, and everything it needs
33|d81b|  from a model arrives through [rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi).
34|3def|  
35|622c|  It grew up inside [leela](https://github.com/vedicreader/leela), where it was already
36|5899|  written to this seam -- nothing in it ever imported the IDE -- and now stands on its own,
37|0fab|  with leela as its first consumer. It also ships its own two frontends, because a brain
38|f06e|  nobody can talk to is hard to judge: a terminal app and an MCP server, both built on the
39|721f|  same `Host`.""")

49|bb9a|  | `01_runtime` | `ramabana.runtime` | the rishi adapter, usage, native diagnostics, compaction |
50|2272|  | `02_tools` | `ramabana.tools` | `Host`, `LocalHost`, the tools, skills, extensions, sub-agents |

53|d208|  | `05_cli` | `ramabana.cli` | the terminal app, on [teleprint](https://github.com/answerdotai/teleprint) |
54|cba2|  | `06_mcp` | `ramabana.mcp` | the same tools, served over MCP |
55|3def|  
56|5ec0|  Every model runtime -- LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp and hosted providers -- arrives through
57|d61d|  `rishi.Chat`. Ramabana owns agent policy, not provider-specific model loops.""")

30|c27c|  md("""ramabana is the *brain* of a coding agent, and nothing else. It has no editor, no
31|78e4|  frontend and no opinion about where it is running: everything it needs from the
32|7e70|  application around it arrives through one protocol, `Host`, and everything it needs
33|d81b|  from a model arrives through [rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi).
34|3def|  
35|622c|  It grew up inside [leela](https://github.com/vedicreader/leela), where it was already
36|5899|  written to this seam -- nothing in it ever imported the IDE -- and now stands on its own,
37|0fab|  with leela as its first consumer. It also ships its own two frontends, because a brain
38|f06e|  nobody can talk to is hard to judge: a terminal app and an MCP server, both built on the
39|721f|  same `Host`.""")

50|2272|  | `02_tools` | `ramabana.tools` | `Host`, `LocalHost`, the tools, skills, extensions, sub-agents |

26|fc53|  md("""# ramabana
27|3def|  
28|b026|  > rama's arrow. a harness that does not miss.""")
29|3def|  
30|c27c|  md("""ramabana is the *brain* of a coding agent, and nothing else. It has no editor, no
31|78e4|  frontend and no opinion about where it is running: everything it needs from the
32|7e70|  application around it arrives through one protocol, `Host`, and everything it needs
33|d81b|  from a model arrives through [rishi](https://github.com/vedicreader/rishi).
34|3def|  
35|622c|  It grew up inside [leela](https://github.com/vedicreader/leela), where it was already
36|5899|  written to this seam -- nothing in it ever imported the IDE -- and now stands on its own,
37|0fab|  with leela as its first consumer. It also ships its own two frontends, because a brain
38|f06e|  nobody can talk to is hard to judge: a terminal app and an MCP server, both built on the
39|721f|  same `Host`.""")
40|3def|  
41|aa5a|  md("""## What is in it
42|3def|  
43|ce2d|  The nbdev source is seven notebooks, and each one is exactly one module -- the page you
44|7e0d|  read and the module you import are the same thing.
45|3def|  
46|de3e|  | notebook | module | owns |
47|cd2c|  |---|---|---|
48|450d|  | `00_core` | `ramabana.core` | errors, environment, and which model runs which job |
49|bb9a|  | `01_runtime` | `ramabana.runtime` | the rishi adapter, usage, native diagnostics, compaction |
50|2272|  | `02_tools` | `ramabana.tools` | `Host`, `LocalHost`, the tools, skills, extensions, sub-agents |
51|9c04|  | `03_agent` | `ramabana.agent` | approvals, the activity feed, `Agent`, inline completion |
52|d0f4|  | `04_testing` | `ramabana.testing` | a full-capability host and the backend doubles |
53|d208|  | `05_cli` | `ramabana.cli` | the terminal app, on [teleprint](https://github.com/answerdotai/teleprint) |
54|cba2|  | `06_mcp` | `ramabana.mcp` | the same tools, served over MCP |
55|3def|  
56|5ec0|  Every model runtime -- LiteRT, MLX, llama.cpp and hosted providers -- arrives through
57|d61d|  `rishi.Chat`. Ramabana owns agent policy, not provider-specific model loops.""")
58|3def|  
59|62dc|  md("""## Install
60|3def|  
61|80ec|  ```sh
62|1e1e|  pip install ramabana                 # the harness
63|e51b|  pip install 'ramabana[cli]'          # ...and the terminal app
64|5014|  pip install 'ramabana[mcp]'          # ...and the MCP server
65|ffd4|  pip install 'ramabana[all]'
66|d341|  ```
67|3def|  
68|4a48|  A model is not bundled. `rishi` fetches one on first use, and which one is a routing
69|34bd|  decision -- see [core](00_core.ipynb).""")

125|2479|  md("""## One hard problem, end to end
126|3def|  
127|8d7a|  Everything above is hermetic. Everything below is not: it runs a real agent, over this real
128|e80d|  repository, against the real internet, and the cells are marked `eval: false` so neither CI
129|fdab|  nor the docs build tries to. **The outputs shown are real**, captured on an Apple silicon
130|5e26|  laptop and saved here.
131|3def|  
132|6273|  The problem is deliberately one that no single tool answers. Half of it is in this repo and
133|b172|  only a code index can find it; the other half is a price on a supermarket website that
134|30ec|  blocks scrapers; and the last line needs both halves at once.
135|3def|  
136|1b94|  Routing is the point. The turn drives a twenty-three tool loop and goes to a hosted model;
137|7658|  every cheap job -- the labels, the summaries, the inline completions, the compaction
138|f3b7|  checkpoint that keeps a long conversation inside its window -- stays on a local MLX model and
139|c355|  never leaves the machine.""")
140|3def|  
141|e315|  code("""#| eval: false
142|6ca4|  from ramabana.agent import Agent
143|bd14|  from ramabana.tools import LocalHost
144|3def|  
145|f73f|  host = LocalHost(['..'], web=True)          # this repository, and the network
146|fc20|  host.wait_index(600)                        # let Kosha finish, so search is semantic
147|3def|  
148|c001|  agent = Agent(host, model='gpt-mini', extensions=False)
149|47f8|  for job in ('inline', 'completion', 'classify', 'summary', 'subagent'):
150|41b6|      agent.routing.set('ornith-9b', job)
151|194e|  agent.start() is not None, agent.note, len(agent.tools)""",
152|1c6f|       out="(True, 'gpt-mini · cloud · 1050k ctx · 23 tools', 23)")
153|3def|

158|8651|       stdout="""turn        gpt-mini · cloud · 1050k ctx
159|0c96|  inline      ornith-9b · local · 32k ctx
160|d8ff|  completion  ornith-9b · local · 32k ctx
161|f91a|  classify    ornith-9b · local · 32k ctx
162|85de|  summary     ornith-9b · local · 32k ctx
163|017f|  subagent    ornith-9b · local · 32k ctx""")

168|5659|   ('remote', 'openai/gpt-5.6-luna')]""")
169|3def|  
170|ef7c|  md("""Now the question:""")
171|3def|  
172|e315|  code("""#| eval: false
173|81a8|  TASK = (\"Two facts, then one line of arithmetic.\\n\"
174|1ae5|          \"1. In this repository, find the constant the compactor holds back for the model's reply, \"
175|65e1|          \"and say what it is called and what it is set to.\\n\"
176|2153|          \"2. Find what Arnott's Tim Tam Original 200g costs at Coles right now, in AUD.\\n\"
177|f736|          \"Finish with one line: the constant, the price, and how many packs those tokens would \"
178|cdeb|          \"buy at $0.001 per token.\")
179|3def|  
180|17e4|  answer = agent.ask(TASK)
181|1baa|  print(answer)""",

183|ab8d|  2. Arnott’s Tim Tam Original 200g costs **AUD $6.00** at Coles. ([Coles](https://www.coles.com.au/product/arnott's-tim-tam-chocolate-biscuits-original-200g-329607))
184|3def|  
185|8c98|  **`RESERVE` (16,384 tokens) × $0.001/token = $16.384 ÷ $6.00 = 2.7307 packs** (2 whole packs).""")
186|3def|  
187|1301|  md("""Both halves are right, and both were *found* rather than recalled. `RESERVE = 16_384` really
188|e206|  is the compactor's output reserve in `ramabana/runtime.py`, and $6.00 really is the shelf
189|c28a|  price -- fetched, not remembered from training.
190|3def|  
191|ec92|  The turn is auditable afterwards, which is the part that matters more than the answer:""")

213|8980|  of it to be a page, and hands the model the page's `schema.org` JSON-LD alongside the prose.
214|f657|  That block is a standard, not a selector for one shop:""")

237|8f5f|  md("""## In a terminal
238|3def|  
239|80ec|  ```sh
240|b348|  ramabana --root . --model gpt-mini
241|d341|  ```
242|3def|  
243|a64c|  A transcript of blocks, a status bar, and one line to type in. Tool calls are foldable blocks
244|c850|  rather than lines, writes stop for approval, and every slash command is the agent's own -- see
245|12e3|  [cli](05_cli.ipynb).
246|3def|  
247|4f60|  The same task, without the terminal, for a pipe:
248|3def|  
249|80ec|  ```sh
250|8231|  $ ramabana --model gpt-mini --approve auto --prompt "$TASK"
251|2b6b|  1. **Constant:** `RESERVE`, set to **16,384 tokens** — headroom for the model's reply and tool results.
252|c369|  2. **Coles price:** Arnott's Tim Tam Original 200g is **A$6.00**.
253|3def|  
254|2c58|  **`RESERVE` (16,384 tokens) × A$0.001 = A$16.384 ÷ A$6.00 = 2.7307 packs (2 whole packs).**
255|d341|  ```
256|3def|  
257|ac18|  Running the turn on the local model instead is one flag, and the reply is the reply -- a
258|a40d|  template-primed reasoning model's deliberation never reaches the transcript:
259|3def|  
260|80ec|  ```sh
261|b732|  $ ramabana --model ornith-9b --prompt 'Reply with exactly the word: pong'
262|f3d5|  pong
263|6d10|  ```""")

271|693d|  The same tools, served to another agent: read-only by default, writes behind `--write`, and
272|d341|  `--model` adds an `ask` tool that runs a whole Ramabana turn and returns just its answer --
273|649e|  see [mcp](06_mcp.ipynb).""")

38|8627|  page read in one session is gone by the next, and the code index and the reading are two

101|3b35|  class FossickCart(Cart):
102|5047|      """A real, logged-in Chrome, driven through `fossick.shop`.
103|3def|  
104|3134|      The session is opened on first use and then reused. `fossick.shop()` picks up a tab an
105|5a59|      earlier call left on the same site instead of piling up another one, so moving to a second
106|34cc|      store and back does not lose the first trolley.
107|3def|  
108|27cf|      Nothing here logs in. Both of the stores this was written for refuse a fresh automated
109|328c|      session -- one is bot-walled, the other is members-only -- so the browser is the one the
110|4599|      person already uses, and the agent is a hand on it rather than a client of its own.
111|d30b|      """

121|3cfe|          elif url: self._s.open(url)

130|3def|

153|874f|  #: Two stores, because the interesting case is a run that spans both: a supermarket for the
154|9b48|  #: staples and a co-op box scheme for the fruit.
155|cdef|  CATALOGUE = {
156|8f1b|      'coles.com.au': [('Full Cream Milk 2L', 3.60), ('Sourdough Loaf 680g', 6.00),
157|21bf|                       ('Free Range Eggs 12pk', 8.50), ('Baby Spinach 120g', 4.00),
158|246a|                       ('Extra Virgin Olive Oil 750ml', 12.00), ('Bananas Cavendish 1kg', 4.90)],
159|fd83|      'ceresfairfood.org.au': [('Seasonal Fruit Box - Medium', 39.00), ('Seasonal Veg Box - Medium', 45.00),
160|d72e|                               ('Organic Lemons 500g', 6.50)],
161|50db|  }

164|550d|  class FakeCart(Cart):
165|91cc|      "A cart with a fixed catalogue and no browser: what the tests and the docs shop at."
166|3def|  
167|52e7|      def __init__(self, catalogue=None, url='https://www.coles.com.au'):
168|54c8|          self.catalogue = dict(catalogue or CATALOGUE)
169|745f|          self._url, self._trolley, self._found = url, [], []
170|3def|  
171|c840|      @property
172|d55f|      def where(self): return self._url
173|3def|  
174|7629|      def _store(self):
175|6fee|          return next((v for k, v in self.catalogue.items() if k in self._url), [])
176|3def|  
177|b1dd|      def open(self, url):
178|4bc6|          self._url, self._found = str(url), []
179|7b98|          return self._url
180|3def|  
181|136d|      def _rows(self, query=''):
182|91ed|          q = str(query).lower()
183|cfb1|          return [dict(i=i, title=t, price=f'${p:.2f}', url=f'{self._url}/p/{i}')
184|ef05|                  for i, (t, p) in enumerate(tp for tp in self._store() if q in tp[0].lower())]
185|3def|  
186|9f8f|      def find(self, query, limit=MAX_PRODUCTS):
187|8aa6|          self._found = self._rows(query)[:int(limit)]
188|b20f|          return self._found
189|3def|  
190|2a96|      def _match(self, want):
191|7b75|          """Index against the last search; a title against the whole store.
192|3def|  
193|97ef|          The real one re-reads the products on the page for every add, so a title that is not in
194|edc7|          the last search still resolves as long as the store stocks it -- which is what lets an
195|0156|          agent add by the exact title it just read back. An index cannot work that way: it only
196|47b0|          means anything relative to the search that produced it.
197|d12c|          """
198|f2ca|          page = self._found or self._rows()
199|0c9e|          if isinstance(want, int) or str(want).isdigit():
200|ce1a|              hit = next((p for p in page if p['i'] == int(want)), None)
201|05ee|              if hit is None: raise CartError(f'no product #{want}; the page has {len(page)}')
202|7446|              return hit
203|492d|          w = str(want).lower()
204|456c|          for pool in (page, self._rows()):
205|2f90|              for test in (lambda t: w == t.lower(), lambda t: w in t.lower()):
206|f460|                  if (hits := [p for p in pool if test(p['title'])]):
207|c082|                      return min(hits, key=lambda p: len(p['title']))
208|8e2b|          raise CartError(f'no product matching {want!r} at {self._url}. '
209|62c1|                          f'Stocked: {[p["title"] for p in self._rows()]}')
210|3def|  
211|9239|      def add(self, item, qty=1, variant=None):
212|9b73|          it, qty = self._match(item), int(qty)
213|21b7|          before = self.total()
214|3043|          line = next((l for l in self._trolley if l['title'] == it['title']), None)
215|086e|          if line: line['qty'] += qty
216|18db|          else: self._trolley.append(dict(i=len(self._trolley), title=it['title'], price=it['price'], qty=qty))
217|7052|          after = self.total()
218|13af|          return dict(ok=after != before, item=it, qty=qty, before=before, after=after)
219|3def|  
220|5721|      def lines(self): return list(self._trolley)
221|3def|  
222|2b9c|      def total(self):
223|fa6e|          n = sum(l['qty'] for l in self._trolley)
224|a5a4|          sub = sum(float(l['price'].lstrip('$')) * l['qty'] for l in self._trolley)
225|014d|          return dict(count=n, subtotal=f'${sub:.2f}')
226|3def|  
227|3f65|      def remove(self, line):
228|4a3a|          it = self._match(line)
229|4146|          self._trolley = [l for l in self._trolley if l['title'] != it['title']]
230|a40a|          return dict(ok=True, removed=it['title'], after=self.total())
231|3def|  
232|04f6|      def stores(self): return {k: 'fake catalogue' for k in self.catalogue}''')

249|df36|  code('''#| export
250|57b4|  def cart_tools(cart):
251|b50d|      "The trolley, as tools. `cart_add` and `cart_remove` are in `WRITE_TOOLS`: they spend money."
252|3def|  
253|6adb|      def cart_stores() -> str:
254|d081|          "The stores whose search and trolley pages are known, and anything worth knowing about each."
255|7423|          try: return clip('\\n'.join(f'{k}  {v}' for k, v in cart.stores().items()))
256|0181|          except Exception as e: return f'could not list stores: {agent_err(e)}'
257|3def|  
258|4a9f|      def cart_open(url: str) -> str:
259|9664|          "Point the shopping session at a store, or at one product page. Do this before searching."
260|40bf|          try: return f'now at {cart.open(url)}'
261|a6ff|          except Exception as e: return f'could not open {url}: {agent_err(e)}'
262|3def|  
263|e532|      def cart_find(query: str, limit: int = 10) -> str:
264|c233|          """Search the store you are on. Returns numbered products; the number is what `cart_add` takes.
265|3def|  
266|c52e|          Search one item at a time and read the titles back before adding -- supermarket search
267|8d41|          is fuzzy, and 'milk' matches oat milk, condensed milk and a milk frother.
268|d12c|          """
269|faf8|          try:
270|da90|              rows = cart.find(query, int(limit))
271|aff0|              if not rows: return f'no products matching {query!r} at {cart.where}'
272|b35d|              return clip('\\n'.join(f"{r['i']:>3}  {r['price'] or '?':>8}  {r['title']}" for r in rows))
273|55cf|          except Exception as e: return f'search failed: {agent_err(e)}'
274|3def|  
275|e8b5|      def cart_add(item: str, qty: int = 1, variant: str = '') -> str:
276|3aa7|          """Put a product in the trolley. `item` is a number from `cart_find`, or an exact title.
277|3def|  
278|3723|          The result says whether the trolley actually moved. `ok=false` means it did not and the
279|03e8|          item is NOT in the cart; `ok=null` means the site gave no signal to check against, so
280|5826|          confirm with `cart_show` before telling the user it is done.
281|d12c|          """
282|faf8|          try:
283|3e3f|              r = cart.add(item, qty=int(qty), variant=variant or None)
284|b897|              ok = r.get('ok')
285|ffca|              state = 'added' if ok else ('UNVERIFIED' if ok is None else 'DID NOT ADD')
286|a629|              title = (r.get('item') or {}).get('title', item)
287|0d19|              return clip(f"{state}: {qty} x {title}\\ntrolley now {json.dumps(r.get('after'))}"
288|15f9|                          + (f"\\n{r.get('error')}" if r.get('error') else ''))
289|34fa|          except Exception as e: return f'could not add {item!r}: {agent_err(e)}'
290|3def|  
291|639f|      def cart_show() -> str:
292|1d4a|          "Read the trolley back: every line, and the count and subtotal."
293|faf8|          try:
294|9f95|              ls, t = cart.lines(), cart.total()
295|16b4|              body = '\\n'.join(f"{l.get('qty', 1)} x {l.get('title')}  {l.get('price', '')}" for l in ls)
296|aa24|              return clip(f"{t.get('count')} items, subtotal {t.get('subtotal')}\\n{body}")
297|1509|          except Exception as e: return f'could not read the trolley: {agent_err(e)}'
298|3def|  
299|f78d|      def cart_remove(line: str) -> str:
300|9818|          "Take one line out of the trolley, by its number in `cart_show` or by exact title."
301|d20c|          try: return clip(json.dumps(cart.remove(line), default=str))
302|003e|          except Exception as e: return f'could not remove {line!r}: {agent_err(e)}'
303|3def|  
304|0357|      return [cart_stores, cart_open, cart_find, cart_add, cart_show, cart_remove]''')

54|3def|  
55|d092|  - `ramabana.tools.LocalHost` — a `Host` over real folders and a live namespace in-process:
56|1499|    sandboxed path resolution (`..` and symlinks resolved *before* the check), automatic
57|1d67|    `Kosha.sync` in a daemon thread, repo-first semantic + keyword search across the open
58|f256|    repository and installed packages, `ast`-based symbols and peers, notebook cells, and a
59|a635|    persistent exec namespace. The reference implementation, and what both frontends run on.
60|1ce5|  - `ramabana.cli` — a terminal app on [teleprint](https://github.com/answerdotai/teleprint).
61|d07f|    Transcript of foldable blocks, live status bar, streaming replies, tool calls as blocks,
62|2a79|    and the approval gate on the input line. `ramabana` and `ramabana -p 'one question'`.
63|53ba|  - `ramabana.mcp` — the same tools served over MCP, read-only by default, plus an `ask` tool
64|065a|    that runs a whole Ramabana turn when a model is configured. `ramabana-mcp`.
65|fdc4|  - `ramabana.testing.FullHost` — a host with *every* capability present over a throwaway
66|2678|    folder, including a research-memory index and a web that returns the pages it was given,
67|6959|    so the whole tool surface has somewhere to be tested. Its release check loads a real MLX
68|6896|    model through rishi and verifies all 28 tool functions and all 28 compiled tool schemas.
69|9282|  - `ramabana.runtime.answer_only` — strips a reasoning model's thinking from a one-shot reply.
70|d6da|  - `ramabana.runtime.prefills_think` / `ThinkFilter` — the streaming half of the same problem.
71|d1a2|    `prefills_think` asks a model's own chat template whether it opens a `<think>` block and
72|28e4|    leaves the model to close it; `ThinkFilter` drops that block out of a streamed turn, and
73|bac6|    re-arms at every tool call because such a template opens a fresh thought per step.
74|d084|  - `ramabana.tools.ld_json` — a page's `schema.org` JSON-LD blocks, which is where a product
75|a816|    page actually states its price. `LocalHost.read_url` now prepends them to the prose.
76|d5dd|  - `mini-coder-4b` (`mlx-community/mini-coder-4b-OptiQ-4bit`) joins the MLX table and becomes
77|48c4|    the default for inline `completion`: a 4B trained on code finishes a line better, and
78|234c|    faster, than a general 9B. Every other cheap job stays on the default local model.
79|3def|  
80|e7f0|  ### Fixed
81|3def|  
82|a7f3|  - **Reasoning models broke every cheap job.** `classify`, `summarise`, `Completer` and
83|f5ba|    compaction all read a one-shot reply as data, and all four returned the model's `<think>`
84|649c|    block instead of its answer. `Backend.oneshot` now strips it, including the unpaired
85|5f4e|    closing tag that is what actually arrives when the chat template opens the block in the
86|38b4|    prompt.
87|af1f|  - **Inline completion could insert prose into your file.** A small model asked for bare code
88|71f9|    explains itself first and then opens a fence the token cap cuts off before it closes;
89|9258|    `_clean` took the whole reply. It now keeps only what follows an unterminated fence, and
90|3efc|    suggests nothing when there is nothing but prose.
91|2701|  - `nbdev-export` works again (it raised `TypeError` in `nbdev/maker.py`), is idempotent, and
92|fd1b|    the custom `tools/export.py` that had replaced it is gone. `nbdev-clean` is a no-op,
93|ce2f|    `nbdev-test` executes every notebook, and generated modules carry the `AUTOGENERATED`
94|7816|    header, real `__all__` lists, module docstrings and doclinks again.
95|3fb8|  - Relative imports in exported cells (`from .core import ...`), which `nbdev-export` refuses.
96|d011|  - **A streamed turn leaked the model's thinking into the reply.** Rishi's splitter waits for an
97|e6dd|    opening `<think>` to know it is inside a thought, so a model whose chat template writes that
98|8927|    tag into the generation prompt — Ornith-1.0-9B, among others — never emits one, and its
99|5eda|    deliberation arrived as ordinary reply text with a stray `</think>` in the middle of it.
100|99a4|    `_stream` now filters the structured chunk stream and renders what is left with Rishi's own
101|fbf8|    formatter. This was the release's one *Known* limitation, and it is gone.
102|8c74|  - **A cheap job could not answer at all inside its own budget.** `classify` allows thirty-two
103|5e6c|    output tokens; a reasoning model spends all thirty-two thinking, so there was no answer left
104|6814|    for `answer_only` to uncover. The one-shot conversation is now built with `think=False`,
105|e961|    which closes the template's thinking block in the *prompt* — the model answers immediately.
106|adaf|  - **The first cheap job capped every one after it.** `_oneshot_chat` is reused across jobs and
107|92cc|    was constructed with the first caller's `max_output_tokens`, so a 32-token `classify` left a
108|1fb7|    32-token ceiling behind and the next `summarise` came back cut off mid-sentence. Each call
109|dec2|    now passes its own cap explicitly.
110|e22b|  - **`read_url` could not read a page that renders in the browser.** A site that turns away
111|ad73|    scrapers answers `200 OK` with an empty shell rather than an error, so escalating on the
112|557c|    status code never fires. `LocalHost.read_url` judges the extracted *text* instead and
113|5588|    escalates to a real browser only when there is too little of it to be a page.
114|8dd4|  - `local_ctx('ornith-9b')` silently returned the fallback window: the table keyed it
115|5acf|    `ornith_9b`, with an underscore, while the model alias has a hyphen.
116|3def|

119|3e5d|  - Every notebook is a literate page: sections with exported summaries that assemble into the
120|40a5|    module docstring, and executable examples that double as the tests — including the terminal
121|72f0|    UI, asserted against a headless terminal emulator, and the MCP server, asserted through
122|94b5|    real `list_tools`/`call_tool` round trips.
123|4436|  - `nbs/index.ipynb` ends on one real problem solved end to end: a routed agent over this
124|f71b|    repository and the live web, finding a constant with the code index and a supermarket price
125|6ed7|    through a browser, and closing on arithmetic that needs both. The turn runs on a hosted
126|af21|    model, every cheap job on a local MLX one. Those cells are `eval: false` with their real
127|1de3|    outputs stored, so neither CI nor the docs build needs a GPU or a network.

1|2ecc|  """The coding agent, which is now `ramabana` rather than a copy of it kept here.
2|3def|  
3|4f71|  This package was a fork. The harness lived in `ramabana`, leela vendored it, and for a
4|14f5|  while that was cheaper than the dependency -- until the two copies drifted far enough that
5|4b57|  each had fixes the other did not. leela's copy had grown `run_shell`, exact-text editing,
6|56e8|  `grep`, the `ERROR:` convention and `AGENTS.md`; ramabana's had grown a vault, a shopping
7|fd86|  cart, a real filesystem `Host`, an MCP server and a per-turn usage ledger. Neither was
8|270e|  "the" harness, which is the failure mode a fork always ends in.
9|3def|  
10|4cd8|  They are merged, `ramabana` is the agent core, and this package is now the seam: the same
11|b2eb|  five module paths leela has always imported, each one an alias for the module that
12|4e59|  actually holds the code.
13|3def|  
14|16a4|  - `leela.agent.core`     -> `ramabana.core`     -- the error type, the environment, model routing.
15|d52f|  - `leela.agent.runtime`  -> `ramabana.runtime`  -- native capture, the context window, the backends.
16|eb1b|  - `leela.agent.tools`    -> `ramabana.tools`    -- `Host` and every tool built on it.
17|42d4|  - `leela.agent.agent`    -> `ramabana.agent`    -- the turn: briefing, approvals, activity, `Agent`.
18|cbba|  - `leela.agent.testing`  -> `ramabana.testing`  -- the doubles: a host with no disk, backends with no model.
19|3def|  
20|bd2c|  Aliasing the modules rather than re-exporting their public names is deliberate. leela
21|8aaa|  reaches for private helpers -- `tools._cmds`, `tools._edits`, `tools._apply_edits` in
22|1b9a|  `app.py` -- and a hand-written re-export list would have to be kept in step with them,
23|a843|  which is the drift this merge exists to end. There is exactly one object per module and
24|9929|  both names point at it.
25|3def|  
26|3aee|  Nothing here imports from `leela`, and nothing in `ramabana` does either: that is what
27|98d6|  keeps the harness testable without an IDE, since `testing.MemHost` is a complete host in a
28|f843|  dict and the whole loop runs against it.
29|c484|  """
30|3def|  
31|1009|  import sys
32|1b6f|  from importlib import import_module
33|3def|  
34|ffe9|  __all__ = ['Host', 'NullHost', 'Hit', 'Backend', 'Agent', 'Completer', 'Approvals', 'Ask',
35|5788|             'ModelSpec', 'Routing', 'AgentError', 'agent_err', 'env']
36|3def|  
37|a6bd|  #: The module paths leela imports, and what each one is an alias for.
38|1870|  _MODULES = ('core', 'runtime', 'tools', 'agent', 'testing')
39|3def|  
40|2807|  from ramabana.core import AgentError, agent_err, env
41|3def|  
42|922d|  _lazy = {'Host': ('tools', 'Host'), 'NullHost': ('tools', 'NullHost'), 'Hit': ('tools', 'Hit'),
43|d279|           'Backend': ('runtime', 'Backend'), 'Agent': ('agent', 'Agent'),
44|4993|           'Completer': ('agent', 'Completer'), 'Approvals': ('agent', 'Approvals'),
45|8f27|           'Ask': ('agent', 'Ask'), 'ModelSpec': ('core', 'ModelSpec'),
46|e7c1|           'Routing': ('core', 'Routing')}
47|3def|  
48|3def|  
49|e81a|  def _alias(name):
50|1ee3|      "Register `ramabana.<name>` under `leela.agent.<name>` so both import paths work."
51|25dd|      mod = import_module(f'ramabana.{name}')
52|6c35|      sys.modules[f'{__name__}.{name}'] = mod
53|e8cd|      setattr(sys.modules[__name__], name, mod)
54|ccca|      return mod
55|3def|  
56|3def|  
57|1d52|  # `core` is cheap and everything else needs it; the rest wait, because `runtime` reaches
58|c804|  # for rishi, which loads a local engine or a cloud client. Asking for `leela.agent.Host`
59|5a80|  # must not pay for that.
60|8509|  _alias('core')
61|3def|  
62|3def|  
63|8738|  def __getattr__(name):
64|a3cd|      "Alias a submodule, or import one of the heavy names, on first touch."
65|12b7|      if name in _MODULES: return _alias(name)
66|f597|      if name in _lazy:
67|41b8|          mod, attr = _lazy[name]
68|170e|          return getattr(_alias(mod), attr)
69|0d4d|      raise AttributeError(f'module {__name__!r} has no attribute {name!r}')
70|3def|  
71|3def|  
72|cb67|  def __dir__(): return sorted(set(globals()) | set(_lazy) | set(_MODULES))

1|a336|  """Source text of the browser assets and the web layer, as single strings.
2|3def|  
3|4668|  A large part of the suite asserts on the *text* of what leela ships to the browser --
4|2fdc|  that a keybinding exists, that a CSS class is defined, that a route renders a given id.
5|95fe|  Those assertions were each reading one file:
6|3def|  
7|189a|      JS = (ROOT/'leela/static/lee-ide.js').read_text()
8|3def|  
9|4695|  which quietly pins the architecture: `lee-ide.js` is one 6,000-line file *because* ~200
10|5e3b|  assertions say so, and the same for `app.py`. Splitting either one would fail a
11|f027|  hundred tests that have no opinion about file layout at all.
12|3def|  
13|5662|  Reading a whole tree instead keeps the assertions honest about what they actually mean --
14|72e2|  "the browser is served this behaviour", not "this behaviour lives in this file". A module
15|72b7|  can move, split or be renamed without touching a single test; deleting the behaviour still
16|c4e9|  fails, which is what the assertions are for.
17|3def|  
18|f4fa|  Everything here is read once at import and cached, so the whole suite pays for one pass
19|cb47|  over the tree rather than one per test module.
20|c484|  """
21|3def|  
22|6041|  from functools import cache
23|bcb0|  from pathlib import Path
24|3def|  
25|7d20|  __all__ = ['ROOT', 'JS', 'CSS', 'EDITOR', 'TERM', 'SERVER', 'AGENT', 'read', 'tree_text']
26|3def|  
27|53cf|  ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
28|3def|  
29|1cd0|  # Sorted so the concatenation is byte-identical between runs and machines: a test that
30|108b|  # reports a character offset or slices around a match stays reproducible.
31|8e85|  def tree_text(rel, glob):
32|9d25|      "Every `glob` file under `rel`, sorted by path, joined with newlines."
33|fb63|      d = ROOT/rel
34|5ff3|      if not d.is_dir(): return ''
35|8991|      return '\n'.join(p.read_text() for p in sorted(d.rglob(glob)))
36|3def|  
37|3def|  
38|bb95|  @cache
39|e748|  def read(rel):
40|18a0|      "One file's text, cached. Empty string when it does not exist."
41|54bf|      p = ROOT/rel
42|0b14|      return p.read_text() if p.is_file() else ''
43|3def|  
44|3def|  
45|bb95|  @cache
46|fe12|  def _static(glob): return tree_text('leela/static', glob) + '\n' + tree_text('leela/vendor', glob)
47|3def|  
48|bb95|  @cache
49|1da2|  def _server():
50|53d2|      # Every Python module leela ships: the shell in `leela/app.py`, the blocks, and core.
51|b03f|      # Reading the whole tree rather than named files is the point -- a route can move from
52|37c0|      # `app.py` into a block, or a domain module into the block that owns it, without a test
53|f6ca|      # edit, while deleting the behaviour still fails.
54|0193|      return tree_text('leela', '*.py')
55|3def|  
56|3def|  
57|aec5|  # Vendored bundles are minified third-party code (CodeMirror, xterm, htmx). They would add
58|c665|  # ~2MB of noise to every substring search and can produce false positives, so the browser
59|b0b5|  # text is leela's own hand-written assets only -- which is now simply `leela/static`, where
60|f27d|  # it used to be a filename blocklist over one mixed folder. CSS still spans both trees,
61|c7a0|  # because xterm's stylesheet ships as `lee-term.css`.
62|bb95|  @cache

65|3def|

69|bc81|  # module dict means later lookups never reach this function.

74|9681|              'SERVER': _server,
75|4b41|              'AGENT':  _agent}

81|a488|      return v

4|b8a7|  metadata: 
5|c64a|    node_type: memory

9|f1dd|  ---
10|3def|  
11|102a|  As of 2026-08-11, `ramabana` is the agent core and `leela.agent` is a seam over it rather
12|1e26|  than a fork of it. The two had drifted in both directions — leela's copy had `run_shell`,
13|f288|  `replace_text`, `grep`/`ls`, the `ERROR:` failure convention and `AGENTS.md`; ramabana's
14|6b97|  had the vault, the shopping cart, `LocalHost`, MCP, `ThinkFilter` and per-turn usage. Both
15|f7f7|  sides were merged into ramabana, then leela's five modules were replaced with files that
16|8414|  do `sys.modules[__name__] = ramabana.<name>`.
17|3def|  
18|bf7e|  **Why:** each fix had to be made twice and neither copy was authoritative. Aliasing the
19|8cc2|  module object (rather than re-exporting names) matters because leela's `app.py` imports
20|7918|  private helpers — `tools._cmds`, `tools._edits`, `tools._apply_edits` — and a hand-written
21|f0cd|  export list would drift again.
22|3def|  
23|c3dc|  **How to apply:** change harness behaviour in ramabana's **notebooks** and run
24|bd85|  `nbdev-export`; never edit `leela/leela/agent/*.py` except the aliases themselves. leela
25|02fe|  resolves ramabana from `[tool.uv.sources] ramabana = { path = "../ramabana", editable = true }`,
26|1a89|  so the two repos must sit side by side. See [[ramabana-module-map]] and
27|0575|  [[ramabana-env-prefix-is-per-application]].

10|3def|  
11|55a5|  ramabana is an nbdev repo built on **rishi** (not lisette/litellm — that was an earlier,
12|08df|  abandoned design). Notebooks in `nbs/` are the source of truth:
13|3def|  
14|2ab8|  | Notebook | Module | What it holds |
15|cd2c|  |---|---|---|
16|cf0d|  | 00_core | ramabana.core | `AgentError`, `env`/`use_env_prefix`, model tables, routing |
17|583c|  | 01_runtime | ramabana.runtime | native capture, `Usage`, `Compactor`, `Backend` + rishi/fastllm |
18|b9fe|  | 02_tools | ramabana.tools | `Host`, `NullHost`, `LocalHost`, every tool group, `tools_for` |
19|6630|  | 03_agent | ramabana.agent | `Activity`, `Approvals`, `RULES`/`system_prompt`, `Agent`, `Completer` |
20|e2e3|  | 04_testing | ramabana.testing | `MemHost`, `FullHost`, `FakeBackend`, `ScriptedBackend` |
21|dbd7|  | 05_cli | ramabana.cli | terminal frontend (teleprint) |
22|fa63|  | 06_mcp | ramabana.mcp | tools + agent as an MCP server |
23|2ecf|  | 07_vault | ramabana.vault | `VaultHost` over a vishalakshi `Vault` |
24|1ad9|  | 08_shop | ramabana.shop | `FossickCart` over `fossick.shop` |
25|3def|  
26|9875|  **Why:** the previously stored map (00_tools/01_core/02_bash_env/…/10_ui, lisette + FastAPI
27|d37a|  + browser agent) describes a version of this package that no longer exists and sent
28|bb45|  sessions looking for modules that are not there.
29|3def|  
30|5807|  **How to apply:** `uv run --extra dev nbdev-export` after any notebook edit; tests are
31|3631|  `uv run --extra dev python -m pytest tests`. `nbdev-test` currently fails only on
32|4c39|  `05_cli.ipynb`, because teleprint registers signal handlers and nbdev runs notebooks off
33|db00|  the main thread — pre-existing, not a regression. See [[ramabana-is-leelas-agent-core]].

11|0cb2|  `ramabana.core.env(name)` reads `$<ENV_PREFIX><name>` then `$<ENV_FALLBACK><name>`. The
12|c8f9|  defaults are `RAMABANA_` / `LEELA_`, and an application overrides them at startup:
13|8ed2|  `leela/leela/agent/core.py` calls `use_env_prefix('LEELA_', 'RAMABANA_')` before aliasing
14|d08e|  the module, so `$LEELA_MODEL` beats `$RAMABANA_MODEL` inside leela and the reverse holds
15|242e|  everywhere else.
16|3def|  
17|005f|  **Why:** user chose this over hardcoding either order when the merge surfaced that leela's
18|a7df|  copy read `LEELA_` first and ramabana's read `RAMABANA_` first. leela's users already have
19|9b13|  `$LEELA_MODEL` set, but a shared core has no business declaring one of its consumers the
20|6837|  legacy one — and a future third consumer gets its own namespace.
21|3def|  
22|889e|  **How to apply:** any new application on ramabana should call `use_env_prefix` once, at
23|b259|  import of its own seam module, before anything reads config. See
24|ff6b|  [[ramabana-is-leelas-agent-core]].

2|3def|  
3|6288|  Date: 2026-08-12
4|b1c8|  Status: approved, ready to plan
5|3def|  
6|b80f|  ## What this is
7|3def|  
8|6c4c|  `ramabana pyrepl` is one terminal holding two things: a Python prompt whose namespace belongs to
9|cd48|  the person typing, and a Ramabana agent that can read that namespace and build in a layer above
10|885f|  it. Neither can overwrite the other's names. Dhrishti is what makes that true, and it is already
11|b1f4|  written — this is the assembly, not the mechanism.
12|3def|  
13|57c2|  There is prior art on disk. `reference/pyrepl.py` and `reference/cli.py` are a working
14|9137|  implementation from before a merge dropped it, `tests/test_pyrepl.py` pins its contract, and

26|36b3|    sandboxed overlay: reads reach any owner variable, writes land in the agent's own layer, and
27|2a3b|    mutating or deleting an owner binding is refused.

43|8dcb|  parses into `self.base`. The server has to start inside the kernel because the namespace it serves
44|e8ff|  is the kernel's, and it runs on a background thread so it keeps answering during a long cell.

55|0a40|  back to `text/markdown`), and errors their traceback or `ename: evalue`.
56|3def|  
57|af98|  ### `DhrishtiHost(LocalHost)`
58|3def|  
59|93e4|  A ramabana `Host` — so every file, search and web tool is the ordinary one — whose *Python* tools
60|d169|  go over HTTP to the agent half of a dhrishti server:
61|3def|  
62|bdce|  | host method | endpoint |
63|e10f|  |---|---|
64|30c1|  | `run_python` | `/agent/api/exec?scope=overlay` |
65|ee12|  | `inspect_python` | `/agent/api/exec?scope=isolated\|overlay` |
66|0110|  | `list_vars` | `/agent/api/rows?profile=minimal&sort=name` |
67|41f2|  | `agent_log` | `/agent/api/info` → the session notebook path |
68|3def|  
69|8252|  `scopes` is `('isolated', 'overlay')` and `kernel_kind` is `'ipykernel'`, which is how `tools_for`
70|9672|  decides the session tools are present. It takes `base` as its second positional argument and
71|c0a0|  forwards everything else to `LocalHost`, so `web=` and `index=` behave as they do anywhere else.
72|3def|  
73|88c9|  `log_cell(source, outputs=None, cell_type='code')` appends to dhrishti's session notebook: the
74|b6b3|  owner's executed cells as code cells carrying their real outputs, and each turn as
75|06ca|  `**user**` / `**assistant**` markdown. That interleaving is the point — one file is the whole
76|d2b2|  session, and it is the file the earlier run produced.
77|3def|  
78|ab53|  ### `PyreplUi(Ui)`
79|3def|  
80|0516|  The existing terminal surface — blocks, gutters, folding, the status bar, approvals, `/copy`,
81|2bf7|  transcript navigation — with a `mode` of `python` or `agent`. **Python is the default**, because
82|6638|  this is a REPL that has an agent in it rather than an agent that has a REPL in it. `/python` and
83|c085|  `/agent` switch; the prompt label and status colour say which is live. Three keys change meaning in
84|9c2c|  python mode: `tab` completes through the kernel, `ctrl-c` interrupts the running cell rather than the
85|00a7|  model, and `enter` submits only a statement that compiles (see *The Python surface* below).
86|3def|  
87|e080|  Two drivers sit under it. `run_code` executes an owner cell, streams outputs into blocks through
88|1c7f|  `on_output`, and logs the cell. `run_agent` streams a model turn on a worker thread, pumping chunks
89|1ea5|  back over a queue onto the loop, and logs the user prompt and the reply as markdown.
90|3def|  
91|028c|  Agent mode is the ordinary Ramabana surface with nothing removed: the same blocks and gutters,
92|ae1b|  folding, approvals, slash commands, attachments, transcript navigation and status bar. Switching to
93|072d|  python mode changes what a line *means*, not what the terminal can do.
94|3def|  
95|c38d|  ## The Python surface
96|3def|  
97|5a5d|  This is where the terminal has to feel like leela rather than like a pipe, and it is three things.
98|3def|  
99|f5e4|  ### Multi-line input
100|3def|  
101|4b3d|  `Ui.on_key` submits unconditionally on `enter`, and the reference sends a single line — so a typed
102|6bd9|  `for i in range(3):` submits an incomplete statement and returns a SyntaxError. Pasted blocks
103|7979|  survive, because bracketed paste arrives through `on_paste` rather than per-key.
104|3def|  
105|124f|  In python mode, `enter` runs the buffer through `codeop.compile_command`. Three outcomes: it
106|15b2|  compiles, so submit; it is *incomplete*, so insert a newline and show a `... ` continuation prompt;
107|b0e6|  it is *invalid*, so say so at the prompt without paying for a round trip to the kernel. The buffer
108|3706|  already holds newlines and the compositor already places a cursor within a wrapped multi-row prompt
109|3d79|  (`05_cli.ipynb` asserts both), so this is a decision about `enter`, not new buffer machinery.
110|3def|  
111|7091|  An empty line submits a pending block, which is what every Python REPL does and what muscle memory
112|3063|  expects.
113|3def|  
114|e796|  ### Colour
115|3def|  
116|0dd9|  `rich.syntax.Syntax` highlights the input line as it is typed and code cells in the transcript,
117|f05c|  with the existing `GRUVBOX` palette. `rich` and `pygments` are already present through the `cli`
118|eb0f|  extra, so this costs no dependency. Highlighting is applied to the *rendering* only — `log_cell`
119|17e1|  and the transcript's `block_text` keep the plain source, so what `/copy` and the session notebook
120|8baf|  carry is still code you can paste.
121|3def|  
122|cd82|  ### Completion, with the namespace described
123|3def|  
124|84c6|  Two sources, and the split matters:
125|3def|  
126|45bf|  - **The kernel completes.** `complete_request` is IPython's completer with jedi behind it, so it
127|6e11|    knows imports, attribute chains, dict keys and paths. Nothing built on dhrishti could match it:
128|3124|    dhrishti has no completion endpoint — its API is `rows`, `expand`, `grid`, `result`, `history`,
129|2881|    `sessions` — and `rows` only knows top-level bindings.
130|e111|  - **Dhrishti describes.** Each candidate that names something live is annotated from
131|3574|    `/agent/api/rows` (or `/agent/api/expand` for an attribute chain) with its type and shape, so the
132|9dc7|    candidate row reads `df → DataFrame [1200×8]` rather than `df`. That is the inspector experience,
133|0ffa|    and it is the reason the annotation comes from the agent half of the API: describing a namespace
134|ca33|    needs no token.
135|3def|  
136|704a|  The annotation is best-effort. A completion list must never wait on HTTP, so candidates paint
137|1f9e|  immediately and gain their descriptions when the lookup returns; a failed or slow lookup leaves
138|3822|  bare names rather than an empty list.
139|3def|  
140|c973|  ### Entry points
141|3def|  
142|dbb7|  `cli.main` gains a `prompt == 'pyrepl'` dispatch that forwards the current option set. The import
143|8aa2|  lives in the function body so `pyrepl.main` is resolved through the module at call time, which is
144|f9c7|  what lets `tests/test_pyrepl.py` monkeypatch it.
145|3def|  
146|08aa|  ## The two shapes
147|3def|  
148|7019|  **Own kernel** — `ramabana pyrepl`. Starts a `Kernel`, bootstraps dhrishti in it, builds a
149|d8e4|  `DhrishtiHost` on its base and runs the full `PyreplUi`. This process is the owner: it armed the
150|367c|  token, so adopting an agent variable is legitimate here.
151|3def|  
152|3669|  > The one thing in this spec that is **not** in the reference implementation: a `/promote <name>`
153|2714|  > command for own-kernel mode, calling the token-gated `/api/promote`. Without it an agent's
154|fe27|  > variable can never be adopted, which is most of why the layering is worth having — but it is new
155|74dd|  > surface area rather than restored surface area, and it can be cut from the first pass without
156|e601|  > affecting anything else here.
157|3def|  
158|164c|  **Attach** — `ramabana pyrepl --attach <name-or-url>`: locking into a kernel that already has an
159|5b69|  agent session, which is the case that matters when ramabana runs inside leela. A bare name is
160|862b|  resolved against `dhrishti.serving.active()` by the registry entry's `name`, matching leela's
161|7839|  `env_name`; anything with a scheme is taken as the base URL. It builds only the `DhrishtiHost` and
162|ec5e|  an `Agent`, and runs the ordinary `Ui`. No `Kernel`, no python mode, and **the owner token is never
163|5696|  read**. Leela already owns the human's Python surface; ramabana
164|9b23|  is purely the agent working the overlay beside it.
165|3def|  
166|6331|  Attach must **not** call `serve_in_kernel` to discover the port. `_start` is guarded by
167|c362|  `if _server is None`, but the assignments above that guard are not: `_profile`, `_env` and
168|bf50|  `_agent_mode` are reassigned unconditionally, and passing `session_dir`/`agent_session_dir` calls
169|2722|  `set_logging` regardless. Re-serving inside leela's kernel would therefore repoint leela's session
170|5aec|  logs and reset its agent mode — quietly promoting a `readonly` session to `restricted`. Discovery
171|cc4c|  goes through the registry, which is read-only.
172|3def|  
173|87fe|  Promotion in attach mode is not ramabana's to perform. The agent's work is visible in the shared
174|461b|  session notebook and over the same API leela is already watching, and the human promotes from the
175|7e73|  surface that holds the token. Ramabana does not add a request-and-confirm protocol for this; there
176|5515|  is nothing it could do that leela cannot already do better, and a second path to a mutating
177|cdf3|  endpoint is exactly what the token exists to prevent.
178|3def|  
179|ad84|  ## Errors
180|3def|  
181|2d3d|  Every host method returns a string, because a tool cannot raise usefully — a transport failure comes
182|1d21|  back as `agent_err(exc)`, a dhrishti-reported error as its own message, and a successful statement
183|4ea6|  with no value as `(ok)`. A failed bootstrap raises, since a pyrepl with no dhrishti is not a
184|a89f|  degraded pyrepl but a different program. A dead kernel answers `ExecOutcome(ok=False,
185|8320|  error='kernel is not running')` rather than hanging on iopub.
186|3def|  
187|7189|  ## Dependencies
188|3def|  
189|0d31|  `dhrishti` and `jupyter-client` go in a new `pyrepl` extra, imported lazily, so a plain ramabana
190|8c8a|  install is unaffected and the missing-dependency message names the extra — the same shape
191|fca5|  `core.resolve` already uses for rishi's optional runtimes. `teleprint` and `rich` are already
192|6307|  present via `cli`.

1017|3def|  
1018|0615|  Inside leela the kernel already exists and already has an agent session, so pyrepl starts

1065|a020|          f'{", ".join(str(e.get("name")) for e in entries) or "none"}')

1017|3def|  
1018|0615|  Inside leela the kernel already exists and already has an agent session, so pyrepl starts
1019|cc76|  nothing: it finds the running server, builds the host against it, and runs the ordinary
1020|5e49|  terminal with no Python mode. Leela owns the human's prompt; Ramabana is the agent beside it.

1025|0a85|  `agent_session_dir` calls `set_logging` regardless. Re-serving inside leela's kernel would hand
1026|8aef|  back the right port while repointing leela's session logs and resetting its agent mode -- a
1027|734c|  `readonly` session would come back `restricted`. The registry is read-only, so it cannot.
1028|3def|  
1029|07dd|  Promotion is not Ramabana's to perform here. The agent's work is visible in the shared session
1030|cd56|  notebook and over the same API leela is already watching, and the human promotes from the
1031|4d49|  surface that holds the token.

1065|a020|          f'{", ".join(str(e.get("name")) for e in entries) or "none"}')

190|df43|  ## 1. Should `agent_log` be lazy (a property, re-fetched on each empty access) instead of fetched once in `__init__`?
191|3def|  
192|9131|  Decision: no, not now — keep it eager-but-guarded, as fixed above. Reasoning:
193|3def|  
194|e564|  - The reviewer's second point (Dhrishti restarting mid-session leaves `agent_log` stale) is real,
195|c045|    but it's a narrower case than it first looks: `serve_in_kernel` is called once per `Kernel`
196|c708|    lifetime (`Kernel._bootstrap`, cell `pyr0009`) and there's no restart path in this module — if
197|0b69|    the kernel dies, `Kernel.alive` goes false and the whole `Kernel` is torn down and replaced, not
198|3d37|    restarted in place. So "Dhrishti restarts but `base` stays the same" isn't a scenario the current
199|755c|    code creates; it would only matter if a future task adds an in-place Dhrishti restart against the
200|a224|    same `base`, which is speculative today.
201|1c6d|  - A lazy property adds real complexity for that speculative case: it would need to distinguish
202|fbfe|    "never fetched" from "fetched and empty" from "fetched, got a value, now must re-check
203|7893|    staleness on every `log_cell` call" — i.e. either a cache-with-TTL or an unconditional refetch
204|e81a|    per `log_cell` call, doubling `log_cell`'s request count for a benefit that only shows up once
205|c8c4|    Task 9's registry can actually replace or restart a live Dhrishti under a `DhrishtiHost` that's
206|949e|    already holding a stale `base`... but at that point the registry is also handing out a new
207|1cfb|    `base`/host per lookup (per the coordinator's own framing: "Task 9 builds a `DhrishtiHost` from
208|85e5|    a registry lookup"), which already gives every lookup a fresh `__init__` and thus a fresh
209|48d1|    `agent_log` — the registry boundary is where re-resolution naturally happens, not inside a
210|cc7e|    single host's lifetime.
211|8e62|  - The one gap eager-fetch-in-`__init__` leaves open — a `DhrishtiHost` constructed while Dhrishti
212|4585|    is mid-startup gets `agent_log = Path('')` permanently, even after the server comes up — is real
213|ca52|    but is exactly what the "construction must not raise" fix targets: the caller gets a host back
214|60ab|    (not an exception) precisely so it can decide to retry, and retrying means constructing a new
215|7422|    `DhrishtiHost` (cheap, no side effects beyond the one GET), which re-fetches. That fits the
216|d994|    registry-lookup pattern Task 9 needs better than adding statefulness to this class.
217|3def|  
218|bb1d|  If a future task needs `agent_log` to self-heal within one long-lived `DhrishtiHost` instance
219|1929|  (no reconstruction), that's the point to revisit this, informed by what Task 9's registry

79|3def|  
80|37f2|  Kept `if src.strip() and not src.endswith('\n\n')`. It is right, for reasons worth recording:
81|3def|  
82|9ab0|  - **Blank line submits the pending block: yes, and it is the `code_state` call that does it,
83|31d2|    not the guard.** After `for i in range(3):` + enter + `    print(i)` + enter the buffer is
84|6749|    `'for i in range(3):\n    print(i)\n'`, and `code_state` of that is `'complete'` under
85|676b|    `'single'` precisely because of the trailing newline. So the next `enter` falls through to
86|d7f5|    `super().on_key` and submits. That is the real Python prompt's behaviour.
87|1e05|  - **`not src.endswith('\n\n')` is an escape hatch, not the mechanism.** It only matters for a
88|6427|    buffer that can never complete: an empty suite body (`for i in range(3):` then enter, enter)
89|290b|    or an unclosed bracket. Without it those grow forever. With it, a second blank line submits
90|b5f8|    and the kernel names the `IndentationError`/`SyntaxError`. Cost: one extra `enter` versus a
91|073e|    real prompt for the empty-suite case. Benefit: an unclosed bracket has a way out at all,
92|1ea5|    which CPython's own REPL does not give you.
93|7d1a|  - **A bare `enter` on an empty buffer does nothing surprising.** `src.strip()` is falsy, so the
94|b519|    branch is skipped entirely and `Ui.on_key` -> `submit()` runs; `submit()`'s `if not line`
95|ba5a|    clears the buffer and returns `None`. No turn, no kernel call.

98|88e3|  prompt's two-enter empty-suite behaviour exactly), but it diverges from the brief for a
99|0756|  pathological case only, and it loses the bracket escape hatch. Not worth it.

152|66cb|  binding dhrishti can report, including `0`, `''`, `[]`, `{}` and `None` itself (which reprs to
153|883c|  the string `'None'`). This means the exact mislabelling the finding describes — a live `0`
154|2b45|  binding read back as `'int'` — cannot happen through the real `/agent/api/rows` endpoint today.

156|cca4|  missing from the JSON altogether (which does happen: the fallback path exists to be defensive
157|1141|  against a different/future transport shape, not against dhrishti's current one).

167|9e15|  `[]` (not a dhrishti-repr string but something else entirely), the old code silently discarded
168|860b|  it in favour of `type`; the new code keeps it.

231|9917|  ## Fix round 2 (1 Important finding — the race introduced by round 1)
232|3def|  
233|7a48|  ### The finding
234|3def|  
235|30be|  Round 1 moved `describe()` off the event loop via `asyncio.to_thread`, which fixed the freeze
236|1309|  but opened a new gap: ordinary character keys are never gated by `self.turn` (`Compositor`
237|5a8d|  only schedules a task when a key handler *returns* a coroutine, and typing a character does
238|3fb0|  not), so a user can keep typing while a prior `tab`'s `describe()` call is still resolving on
239|b7ae|  its worker thread. The old `finally` unconditionally did
240|a223|  `self.matches = annotate(matches, described)`, overwriting whatever the buffer had moved on to
241|9f33|  with candidates computed for a buffer state that no longer existed — with no cancellation and
242|c54b|  no generation/staleness tracking anywhere.
243|3def|  
244|4a1a|  ### The fix
245|3def|  
246|2a45|  `PyreplUi.complete_python` (cell `6491d734`) now captures the buffer's identity — `(buf.text,
247|a8e2|  buf.cursor)` as a tuple — before the first `await`, and a `stale()` closure that compares the
248|b760|  current buffer against it:
249|3def|  
250|0787|  ```python
251|34b9|  identity = (self.buf.text, self.buf.cursor)
252|d080|  def stale(): return (self.buf.text, self.buf.cursor) != identity
253|29cd|  try:
254|f697|      matches, start = await self.kernel.complete(self.buf.text, self.buf.cursor)
255|4e32|      if not matches or stale(): return
256|5445|      common = os.path.commonprefix(matches)
257|46b2|      if len(matches) == 1 or len(common) > self.buf.cursor - start:
258|f741|          self.buf.text = self.buf.text[:start] + common + self.buf.text[self.buf.cursor:]
259|7cb5|          self.buf.cursor = start + len(common)
260|07bc|          identity = (self.buf.text, self.buf.cursor)   # our own edit, not the user moving on
261|1c56|      if len(matches) <= 1:
262|fa5d|          self.matches = None
263|9602|          return
264|258f|      self.matches = list(matches)
265|d256|      self.paint()
266|0595|      described = await asyncio.to_thread(getattr(self.agent.host, 'describe', dict))
267|9531|      if stale(): return   # the buffer moved on while `describe` was in flight; drop it
268|f46b|      self.matches = annotate(matches, described)
269|25a2|  finally:
270|d4e8|      self.turn = None
271|d256|      self.paint()
272|d341|  ```
273|3def|  
274|0757|  **Both awaits are checked**, per the finding's own prompt ("consider whether the bare-names
275|eace|  paint has the same problem"): the kernel round trip (`await self.kernel.complete(...)`) and the
276|8f00|  off-thread `describe()` lookup are independent gaps — the buffer can move on during either
277|5b5c|  without moving on during the other — so a single check placed before both assignments would
278|befd|  miss whichever gap it wasn't adjacent to. I did not find a way to collapse them into one check
279|f29f|  without losing coverage of one gap, so there are two calls to the same `stale()` closure rather
280|7a62|  than one.
281|3def|  
282|d93b|  **The buffer's own self-inflicted edit is not treated as staleness.** When a completion
283|c7bd|  extends the buffer to the shared prefix (`self.buf.text = ...; self.buf.cursor = ...`),
284|c84f|  `identity` is updated to that new state immediately afterward — that edit is this coroutine's
285|a1b4|  own action, not the user moving on, and treating it as staleness would have discarded every
286|7f47|  single-match (and prefix-extending multi-match) completion's own result against itself.
287|3def|  
288|982d|  **The `finally` still always runs.** `self.turn = None` and `self.paint()` happen regardless of
289|561f|  which `return` (early, stale, or normal) was taken, so a discarded completion cannot wedge the
290|86b3|  next `tab` press.
291|3def|  
292|dc7b|  ### The test
293|3def|  
294|d1b8|  Inserted after the round-1 thread-identity test (cell `2aef2cf9`, after `39675662`). Made
295|8679|  deterministic per the finding's own instruction ("a race that usually passes is worse than no
296|1237|  test"): `host.describe` is replaced with a stand-in that blocks on a `threading.Event` until
297|9633|  released. The test:
298|96ee|  1. Clears `ui.matches` explicitly first — `buf.clear()` in earlier cells does not reset it, and
299|41b6|     the first version of this test failed for exactly that reason (see below).
300|9e70|  2. Starts `ui.complete_python()` as a task (`asyncio.ensure_future`, not awaited directly, so
301|0a5a|     the test coroutine can act while it's in flight).
302|a0ab|  3. Polls (`await asyncio.sleep(0.01)` in a loop) until `ui.matches` holds the bare (unannotated)
303|1473|     list — the guaranteed point at which `describe` has been handed to its worker thread and is
304|ff2b|     blocked on the event.
305|dbb6|  4. Simulates the user continuing to type via `ui.on_key(Key('x', char='x'))` — a real keystroke
306|e456|     through the real dispatch path, not a direct buffer mutation, which is exactly the mechanism
307|207a|     the finding describes (character keys are not gated by `self.turn`). This appends to the
308|f81f|     buffer and, synchronously, clears `self.matches` (via `on_key`'s own bottom-of-method
309|a534|     `self.matches = None`) — asserted immediately.
310|84db|  5. Releases the blocked `describe`, awaits the task, and asserts `ui.matches` is still `None`
311|5f74|     and `ui.buf.text` is still `'twovals_x'` — the stale `annotate()` result never landed over
312|f529|     what the keystroke had already cleared.
313|3def|  
314|2442|  **A bug in my first version of this test, caught by running it:** the very first draft did not
315|3209|  reset `ui.matches` before starting, so the assertion at step 3 ("bare, not yet annotated")
316|6bef|  failed immediately against leftover annotated matches from the *previous* test cell (`39675662`
317|9b58|  leaves `ui.matches` populated; only `on_key`/`submit` clear it, not `buf.clear()`). This was a
318|b115|  test bug, not a production-code bug — `uv run nbdev-test` caught it on the first run, I fixed
319|d5bf|  the test by clearing `ui.matches` explicitly at the top, and it then passed.

281|8927|    tag into the generation prompt — Ornith-1.0-9B, among others — never emits one, and its

4|6776|  There is one program, `ramabana`, and a Python prompt is a mode inside it.

6|afee|  ## Why, so you can judge trade-offs the brief does not cover
7|3def|  
8|74e4|  `pyrepl` today duplicates `cli`: its own `amain`, its own key dispatcher, its own `submit`, its own
9|b84a|  `tail`. Every bug the owner hit this session came out of one of those copies drifting from the
10|fc2f|  original: dropped attachments, dropped prompt history, an uncleared completion menu, a missing `/`
11|bdf2|  guard on tab, and a `submit` that returned a block where a coroutine was expected. Two surfaces that
12|7aca|  must stay in step is the defect. Deleting one is the fix, so prefer deleting to adding throughout.

301|9bcc|  One program, one prompt, and two things a line can mean. `/python` starts a kernel of the user's

308|ebca|  kernel and calls `Agent.refresh`, which drops the skill, registry and tool caches and re-briefs
309|3170|  the running turn backend in place -- so the agent's Python becomes Dhrishti's protected overlay
310|f9a8|  mid-session: it reads the namespace being typed into, writes into a layer of its own, and cannot
311|a44a|  rebind a name the owner made.

313|488d|  Everything a Python prompt has to judge -- the kernel, the overlay host, whether a line compiles,
314|639a|  how to colour it -- lives in [pyrepl](11_pyrepl.ipynb), imported on demand so a plain `ramabana`

1|03e2|  # Changelog
2|3def|  
3|1b0a|  ## Unreleased
4|3def|  
5|c691|  Half the sandbox, a row of options, and the terminal app's hands back -- plus a pass over
6|42df|  everything the harness was leaving on the table in the four libraries underneath it.
7|3def|  
8|bc9e|  ### New
9|3def|  
10|c85a|  - `ramabana --python`: a Python prompt whose namespace is yours, with the agent reading it through
11|6277|    Dhrishti's sandboxed overlay and unable to rebind anything it did not create. It is a mode of the
12|410a|    one terminal rather than a second program -- `/python` starts the kernel and takes the line,
13|75c3|    `/agent` hands it back, and everything else about the surface is unchanged. `--attach` locks into
14|4d2b|    a kernel that is already serving, which is how it runs inside leela.
15|3def|  
16|404a|  ### Added
17|3def|  
18|72e8|  - **`ask_memory`**, and `Host.ask` behind it -- ask remembered research a question and get a
19|7d67|    short cited answer rather than the sections. The same trade `delegate_search` makes: reading
20|04bd|    the material yourself costs every section of every candidate document in your context.
21|6faa|    It appears only for a host that implements `Host.ask`.
22|c4b9|  - **Private material is answered on this machine.** When the sections a question retrieved hold
23|b256|    personal information -- decided arithmetically by `vishalakshi.pii`, never by asking a model to
24|0a1c|    read it first -- the answer is computed by a local model under a briefing that forbids it
25|88a9|    repeating any personal detail to the caller. It says what it is holding and what instruction
26|65d3|    would let it answer usefully; the caller sends that back as `instruction` and it gets another
27|6aee|    turn on the same sections. The runtime is checked on the chat object before a character is
28|0474|    sent, so a lent hosted chat is refused rather than trusted, and `pii='off'` is deliberately
29|4254|    not reachable from the far end of a tool call.
30|cd34|  - `Agent.lend_model`'s factory honours the model it is asked for (`Agent._spec_for`), which is
31|4820|    what makes "the local one" mean it.
32|85a9|  - **`Host.capabilities`** -- a host declares which tool groups it supports, and `tools_for`
33|ec2d|    asks before it probes. The probe is the first thing to touch a host, so a capability whose
34|79a8|    answer sits behind a model load is one the probe waits through: `VaultHost` opens its vault
35|13af|    in the background precisely so the tool list does not wait, and `memory_tree('')` then
36|8862|    blocked on the lock that thread holds. 3.0s against a stub, a whole embedding model against
37|ed6b|    a real one, on the first `Agent.tools` access.
38|494a|  - **`Agent.poll_watches`** and `Agent(poll_every=)` -- the tick the watch feature was built
39|34cc|    around and nothing ever called. A turn is the tick, in a daemon thread; whatever fires files
40|e70d|    itself into memory. `VaultHost.connect` is the same move for the entity graph, which
41|85eb|    `research` used to rebuild inline on the one path where the user is definitely waiting.
42|a5c9|  - **`Host.grep`** -- a host with a fast exact matcher answers it, and `LocalHost` does through
43|d6de|    ripgrep, covering exactly the files `walk` yields. The tool read every file through
44|9d21|    `host.read`, and therefore `check`, and therefore a `resolve` per file.
45|cdc7|  - **`Agent.snapshot_tree`** and `SHELL_SNAPSHOT` -- `changes()` keyed on a tool argument named
46|bb14|    `path`, and `run_shell` has none, so a command that rewrote twenty files reported `{}`.
47|359a|  - **`LocalHost(rerank=, rerank_model=)`** -- Kosha's cross-encoder, wired through to both
48|c514|    context calls. It falls back once and stops asking if flashrank cannot fetch its model.
49|44ba|  - **`LocalHost.indexed`** -- per-folder index readiness, so a small repo goes semantic while a
50|18f2|    large one is still syncing. `index_ready` is now "all of them".
51|da98|  - **An `oneshot` routing job**, and `Routing.spec` falling back when a job's model is not
52|7363|    installed here. `inline`, `completion`, `classify` and `summary` take it unless singled out.
53|47e7|  - **`Agent.lend_model`** and `VaultHost(mk_chat=)` -- vishalakshi builds a chat per `ask`, which
54|4e0f|    on a local model is a second copy of an engine already in memory, answering on a different
55|efce|    model from the one being talked to.
56|71af|  - **`core.claude_tags`** and `$RAMABANA_CLAUDE_TAG_TOOLS` -- Claude Code declares tools as an
57|a670|    in-process MCP server and an enterprise-managed configuration forbids every dynamic MCP
58|4f03|    server, so the tools were stripped and the model ran blind. They travel in the system prompt
59|680e|    instead, through Rishi's `tool_mode='tags'`.
60|504f|  - **`LocalHost(read_outside=True)`** -- the sandbox has two halves and only one of them is
61|772b|    usually the point. Confining *writes* stops an agent damaging something nobody opened;
62|2910|    confining *reads* stops it answering a question whose answer is in a sibling checkout or a
63|a550|    library outside the venv. With this on, a read may name any path on the machine and a write
64|d07a|    may not. Enumeration is unchanged either way -- `walk`, and therefore `grep` and
65|c021|    `list_files`, never leave the open folders -- so a read outside is always a path the model
66|c5d0|    already knew, never one it found by looking. `DENY` is the short list of credential paths
67|fcae|    refused regardless, because opening the sandbox is a decision about source and not about
68|0057|    the user's keys. `--read_outside` on both `ramabana` and `ramabana-mcp`.
69|24a0|  - `Host.check` takes `reading=`, and the read-only tools resolve through the new
70|730d|    `tools.readable`, which checks the signature first -- so the flag is a host capability
71|20be|    rather than a tool assumption and a host written before it sees the call it always saw.
72|9376|  - **`cli.Option` / `options_for` / a reworked `ChoiceMenu`** -- the two-choice refactor prompt
73|7460|    became a component. A prompt whose *reading* matters gets a titled row of options above the
74|93c2|    input line, each with the instruction it appends; arrows, digits or the option's own letter
75|340d|    pick one, and cancelling hands the typed line back to the composer instead of dropping it.
76|a098|  - `cli.mk_host`, and `--vault` on both frontends: durable memory through `VaultHost` was
77|48f3|    reachable only by writing Python, so neither frontend could use vishalakshi at all.
78|4adb|  - **Attachments** in `ramabana.cli` -- `MEDIA`, `Attachment`, `media_path`, `media_paths`,
79|85f4|    `attach_refs`, `media_parts`, `media_note`, and `Ui.attach`/`detach`/`attach_row`. A prompt
80|f76a|    now carries up to `MAX_ATTACH` files, images *and* audio, named the way a terminal already
81|51eb|    hands files over: dropped on the window, pasted as a path, or written `@path` in the
82|e4f3|    sentence. Every shape a terminal delivers a drop in resolves to the same attachment --
83|d171|    quoted, bracketed, a `file://` URI, spaces backslash-escaped, several at once -- where
84|e368|    before only a bare unquoted path did, which is why dropping a picture on the prompt
85|2e52|    usually just typed its path. Pictures go out as content parts; *every* attachment is also
86|2f30|    named by absolute path, so a runtime with no ear for audio can still reach a `.wav`
87|7bd5|    through the file tools. Chips above the prompt say what the next message will carry, and
88|a54c|    the turn that named them is the only one that carries them.
89|2055|  - **`Ui.attach_clipboard` and `clipboard_png`**, on `ctrl+v` and `/paste`. Bracketed paste
90|d59c|    carries text and only text, so a copied *image* never arrived as input at all; the picture
91|d580|    has to be asked of the platform (`pngpaste`, `wl-paste`, `xclip`), and a missing helper is
92|e058|    a plain sentence rather than a silent no-op.
93|91ea|  - **`Ui.copy_last`, on `/copy`** -- the newest reply to the system clipboard over OSC 52,
94|c851|    without leaving the prompt for the transcript view to get it.
95|5ada|  - `Ui.note`, `Ui.touch`, and `Ui.enter_transcript`/`leave_transcript`.
96|3def|  
97|e7f0|  ### Fixed
98|3def|  
99|b0d2|  - **`Agent.changes()` was blind to `run_shell`.** It keyed on a tool argument called `path`,
100|ceb5|    and a command names no files: `black .`, a codemod, a `git checkout` can rewrite twenty
101|4cc8|    files and mention none of them, and the answer came back `{}` -- worse than a gap, because
102|4534|    the README points at `changes()` as the thing that knows what moved.
103|7510|  - **`_named` dropped the positional half of a mixed call.** `args = kw if kw else _named(f, a)`,
104|65b3|    so `edit_file('a.py', commands=...)` was recorded with no path -- an unreadable activity line,
105|54eb|    and a file that was never snapshotted, because the path `changes()` looks for is that one.
106|1562|  - **`LocalHost.search` tried its legs in order instead of fusing them**, so a rename whose query
107|58b0|    happened to embed well lost its own call sites. Both run and `fossick.rrf` merges them.
108|cf97|  - **`read_url` promised "(or GitHub file, arxiv paper)" and plain-fetched both.** It routes to
109|16a6|    fossick's own readers now, and escalates through `fetch(auto=True)` -- plain, heavy, stealthy,
110|e75d|    logged-in Chrome -- rather than jumping hand-rolled from plain to a stealth browser.
111|3b12|  - **Kosha was told to sync serially** (`in_parallel=False`, overriding its own default, for no
112|c4f4|    reason anyone wrote down), which is why `index_ready` took minutes and every search until
113|849a|    then was literal.
114|aded|  - **`resolve` checked `runtime_available` for a `vendor/model` name and not for a short one**, so
115|7af0|    `resolve('qwen-4b')` succeeded on a machine with no MLX; the job built a backend, `start()`
116|2502|    failed, and `Agent.oneshot` returned `''`. The cheap jobs did not error -- they stopped
117|be5e|    happening.
118|4037|  - **`LocalHost(roots=())` raised `IndexError` out of `check`.** It is a legal host; it refuses
119|db9a|    paths with an `AgentError` that says why.
120|b716|  - **`ramabana.core` wrote into `sys.modules` at import time**, rearranging `toolslm` for every
121|de9e|    other consumer in the interpreter because somebody imported this library to read a constant.
122|3693|    The shim is installed at the two points that need it.
123|2dda|  - **`scale_numeric` is gone** -- a pandas min-max scaler in the permanent tool list of a general
124|4351|    coding harness, which is what `coding_patterns` says not to do.
125|26d1|  - **`RishiBackend` reached into five Rishi privates** (`_oneshot`, `_sys_pre`, `toolspecs`, `ns`,
126|04c5|    `_recreate_conv`). Rishi grew `Chat.oneshot` and `Chat.reconfigure`; `think=False` now applies
127|427f|    on every runtime rather than only MLX.
128|8276|  - `LlamaBackend` and `FastllmBackend` warn as deprecated aliases for `RishiBackend`.
129|9452|  - `pyproject` refused to install below 3.12 while its classifiers claimed only "Python 3".
130|c1c1|  - **An attached image shredded the rest of the message.** `compose` returns a list of content
131|7731|    parts when there is an image, and `_prepare` then did `list += str` -- which extends a list
132|11e3|    one character at a time. Every multimodal turn reached the model as the image followed by
133|002a|    several hundred single-character parts, with the tool plan and every preflight result
134|aa9d|    scattered among them.
135|b8a5|  - `Approvals` refusals that nobody could be asked about (`mode='off'`, or no listener

265|e7f0|  ### Fixed
266|3def|  
267|a7f3|  - **Reasoning models broke every cheap job.** `classify`, `summarise`, `Completer` and
268|f5ba|    compaction all read a one-shot reply as data, and all four returned the model's `<think>`
269|649c|    block instead of its answer. `Backend.oneshot` now strips it, including the unpaired
270|5f4e|    closing tag that is what actually arrives when the chat template opens the block in the
271|38b4|    prompt.
272|af1f|  - **Inline completion could insert prose into your file.** A small model asked for bare code
273|71f9|    explains itself first and then opens a fence the token cap cuts off before it closes;
274|9258|    `_clean` took the whole reply. It now keeps only what follows an unterminated fence, and
275|3efc|    suggests nothing when there is nothing but prose.
276|2701|  - `nbdev-export` works again (it raised `TypeError` in `nbdev/maker.py`), is idempotent, and
277|fd1b|    the custom `tools/export.py` that had replaced it is gone. `nbdev-clean` is a no-op,
278|ce2f|    `nbdev-test` executes every notebook, and generated modules carry the `AUTOGENERATED`
279|7816|    header, real `__all__` lists, module docstrings and doclinks again.
280|3fb8|  - Relative imports in exported cells (`from .core import ...`), which `nbdev-export` refuses.
281|d011|  - **A streamed turn leaked the model's thinking into the reply.** Rishi's splitter waits for an
282|e6dd|    opening `<think>` to know it is inside a thought, so a model whose chat template writes that
283|0460|    tag into the generation prompt -- Ornith-1.0-9B, among others -- never emits one, and its
284|5eda|    deliberation arrived as ordinary reply text with a stray `</think>` in the middle of it.
285|99a4|    `_stream` now filters the structured chunk stream and renders what is left with Rishi's own
286|fbf8|    formatter. This was the release's one *Known* limitation, and it is gone.
287|8c74|  - **A cheap job could not answer at all inside its own budget.** `classify` allows thirty-two
288|5e6c|    output tokens; a reasoning model spends all thirty-two thinking, so there was no answer left
289|6814|    for `answer_only` to uncover. The one-shot conversation is now built with `think=False`,
290|f256|    which closes the template's thinking block in the *prompt* -- the model answers immediately.
291|adaf|  - **The first cheap job capped every one after it.** `_oneshot_chat` is reused across jobs and
292|92cc|    was constructed with the first caller's `max_output_tokens`, so a 32-token `classify` left a
293|1fb7|    32-token ceiling behind and the next `summarise` came back cut off mid-sentence. Each call
294|dec2|    now passes its own cap explicitly.
295|e22b|  - **`read_url` could not read a page that renders in the browser.** A site that turns away
296|ad73|    scrapers answers `200 OK` with an empty shell rather than an error, so escalating on the
297|557c|    status code never fires. `LocalHost.read_url` judges the extracted *text* instead and
298|5588|    escalates to a real browser only when there is too little of it to be a page.
299|8dd4|  - `local_ctx('ornith-9b')` silently returned the fallback window: the table keyed it
300|5acf|    `ornith_9b`, with an underscore, while the model alias has a hyphen.
