117|6078|  ## Judgement calls
118|3def|  
119|428e|  **`/python` without the extra refuses, naming it.** `PYREPL_MODULES = ('jupyter_client',
120|c499|  'dhrishti')` is checked with `find_spec` before anything is promised. Attempting the import instead
121|d7dd|  would fail inside `Kernel.start` (jupyter_client) or the bootstrap cell (dhrishti), and by then the
122|36d1|  only honest message is a traceback string that does not mention the extra -- and for dhrishti the
123|5e4d|  failure arrives *after* a kernel has been started and must be torn down. The constant is a
124|2905|  module-level tuple so a test can neutralise it in one line, which is how the notebook test runs
125|6704|  without dhrishti installed (`nbs/05_cli.ipynb#pymode02`). `--attach` is resolved in `main` before
126|ce51|  any terminal exists, so a name that does not resolve is a message and exit code 2 rather than a
127|d244|  half-drawn compositor; `ModuleNotFoundError` there is answered with the extra's name too.
128|3def|  
129|cd1b|  **`run_turn` keeps the logging, through one guard rather than two `hasattr`s.** I took the brief's
130|4adb|  option but put the guard in `Ui.log_cell` -- `getattr(self.agent.host, 'log_cell', None)` -- so
131|d56f|  `run_turn` and `run_code` both read as one line each and there is a single place that knows only a
132|ff9c|  `DhrishtiHost` keeps a notebook. The alternative (stop logging agent turns) would break the feature
133|4a89|  the session notebook exists for: the owner's cells and the model's turns interleaved in one
134|bc27|  artifact, which is what leela and the `--attach` case read. The cost is that `run_turn` now requires
135|d3a2|  its `ui` to have `log_cell`; it already requires `attachments`, `stream`, `touch`, `paint`, `say`,
136|e517|  `turn` and `_reply`, so this is not new coupling. I also tightened the assistant-side log to
137|ea7f|  `if blk is not None and ui._reply`: `_reply` is only reset when the first chunk arrives, so a turn
138|4ff9|  that produced nothing would otherwise have logged the *previous* turn's reply. `run_agent` had that
139|39b8|  bug.
140|3def|  
141|6a28|  **`/python` with a kernel already running just switches the mode.** `enter_python` guards the whole
142|f0d0|  start-and-swap block with `if self.kernel is None`, so a second `/python` is idempotent and cannot
143|ee02|  orphan a kernel or re-brief the agent for nothing. **`/agent` with no kernel** switches anyway and
144|aa66|  says `agent mode; no kernel is running` -- it is the resting state, not an error, and refusing it
145|b035|  would make the message about `/agent` when the interesting fact is about `/python`.
146|3def|  
147|7656|  **`--attach` does not imply python mode.** The brief's parameter comment says it does, but an
148|9a57|  attached session has no kernel of ours: `run_code`, `complete_python` and the ctrl+c interrupt all
149|c2d2|  go through `self.kernel`, and `promote` has no owner token to read. So `attach_session` builds the
150|a282|  overlay host, records `self.attached`, and leaves the mode at `agent` -- which is what the old
151|4df2|  `pyrepl.amain` did (it built a plain `Ui` when there was no kernel) and what `PY_GUIDE` promised
152|fdd0|  ("no python mode, no owner token"). `/python` in an attached session answers `attached to <base>:
153|5847|  that Python prompt belongs to whoever started it`. Tracked with an explicit `self.attached` rather
154|50e3|  than sniffing for `host.base`, because after a normal `enter_python` the host has a `base` too.
155|3def|  
156|c85e|  **`--vault` with `--python` or `--attach` is still refused** (exit 2), for the reason the old
157|11fc|  dispatch refused it: `enter_python` replaces the host, so a vault-backed one would be silently
158|175f|  discarded. Pinned in `#poscli01`.

187|82e5|  ## What I could not do, and what to watch
188|3def|  
189|e50d|  - **The lazy imports read `from ramabana.pyrepl import ...`, not `from .pyrepl import ...`.** nbdev
190|7003|    rewrites absolute imports to relative only for *top-level* statements (`maker.update_import`
191|80c1|    filters `cell.parsed_()`, which is the module body), so an indented `from .pyrepl import` in the
192|df32|    notebook would stay relative and fail when the notebook executes the cell. `mk_host`'s
193|efeb|    `from .vault import ...` gets away with it only because no notebook cell ever calls it with
194|bc78|    `vault=True`. Mine run on every keystroke, so absolute is the only form that works in both places.
195|aefd|  - **`--python` indexes the roots twice.** `main` builds a `LocalHost` (which starts a Kosha sync)
196|00c5|    and `enter_python` then builds a `DhrishtiHost` over the same roots, which starts its own. Kosha's
197|0e8a|    sync is incremental and runs on a daemon thread, so the second one is cheap, but it is duplicated
198|7faa|    work that only disappears if `Ui` can move koshas between hosts. Not worth an API for it now.
199|bb90|  - **`enter_python`'s kernel start is not cancellable.** It is spawned as `ui.turn`, so ctrl+c
200|e1ce|    cancels the task, but `Kernel.start`'s `finally` will not have run; a failed start is answered
201|7230|    with `no kernel: ...` and leaves `self.kernel` `None`, which is the case that matters.
202|e042|  - **`Ui.attach_session` is `async` without awaiting anything.** `DhrishtiHost.__init__` makes a
203|b351|    blocking HTTP call; today it is only ever called before the event loop is doing anything else, so
204|ae82|    this is honest but latent. If `/attach` ever becomes a slash command, that call wants
205|c19b|    `asyncio.to_thread`.
206|65ed|  - The orphaned dhrishti kernel from earlier testing was left alone, as instructed.

1|523b|  # Claude instructions
2|3def|  
3|f005|  These are Claude Code's instructions for working *on* this repository. `AGENTS.md` applies to every agent and still holds; this file adds what is specific to Claude Code and to the Answer.AI house behaviour (adapted from `AnswerDotAI/aai-coding`, `prompts/sysp.md` and `prompts/core.md`).
4|3def|  
5|f4ad|  Do not confuse this file with the prompts the package *builds*. `ramabana.agent.system_prompt` assembles a briefing for agents Ramabana runs, and `project_context` reads `AGENTS.md` (not this file) from each open root. Nothing here changes that behaviour; changing it means editing `nbs/03_agent.ipynb`.
6|3def|  
7|278c|  ## Workflow: the notebooks are the source
8|3def|  
9|cc17|  `nbs/*.ipynb` is the source of truth. Every module in `ramabana/` is generated and carries `# AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT!`; so is `README.md` (from `nbs/index.ipynb`), `ramabana/_modidx.py`, `ramabana/__init__.py`, and `nbs/llms.txt`. Never hand-edit a generated file — make the change in the notebook and export.
10|3def|  
11|3081|  Never parse `.ipynb` as JSON. Use `NotebookEdit`, or `fastcore.nbio` (`read_nb`, `write_nb`, `mk_cell`) in code, per `.agents/skills/nbio-notebook-edits/SKILL.md`.
12|3def|  
13|41e2|  The documented commands, from the Develop section of `README.md`:
14|3def|  
15|03a7|      uv sync --all-extras --group dev
16|eba7|      uv run nbdev-export           # notebooks -> ramabana/*.py
17|c980|      uv run nbdev-test             # execute every notebook
18|471d|      uv run pytest                 # the plain-python suite
19|6976|      uv run nbdev-clean            # before committing
20|3def|  
21|ec95|  Use `nbdev-prepare` (hyphen), never `nbdev_prepare`. Run commands in their plain documented form and read the complete output: no `head`, no `tail`, no `2>&1`. This checkout is hatchling, so packaging changes go in `pyproject.toml` under `[tool.hatch.build]`, never `MANIFEST.in`. Installs go through `uv add`, never `pip install`, and never without asking first.
22|3def|  
23|6d80|  `cd` and shell `for` loops are blocked by the safecmd allowlist here. Use absolute paths.
24|3def|  
25|ea9f|  ## Before writing code
26|3def|  
27|1302|  Surface what already exists before implementing anything: invoke the `kosha` skill, and `litesearch` for semantic index queries, ahead of Grep or Read. The answer is usually already in this repo or an installed package. For Python that needs state across calls, use `clikernel` rather than repeated `uv run python`; kosha and clikernel live outside the venv.
28|3def|  
29|69cb|  Match the surrounding design. This codebase uses fastcore selectively — `patch` to spread a class across cells, `delegates` on subclass `__init__`s, `AttrDict`, `L`, `ifnone` — but assigns in `__init__` explicitly rather than reaching for `store_attr`. Docments are the house signature style: one parameter per indented line with a trailing `#` comment, closing `):` at definition indentation. Never strip a docment while refactoring. Docstrings are one line. Comments state constraints the code cannot express, never narrate the next line.
30|3def|  
31|a0b6|  Tests in `tests/` are hand-written pytest with long sentence-style names (`test_private_sections_never_reach_a_hosted_model`), plain `assert`, doubles from `ramabana.testing`, and no test loads a model. Notebooks carry the readable `test_eq` examples; `tests/` asserts contracts in bulk. Keep that division.
32|3def|  
33|e2cf|  ## Partnership, not consultancy
34|3def|  
35|b67a|  Stay divergent. Name the directions you see and your uncertainty, admit the set is incomplete, treat half-formed ideas as leads to pull rather than claims to check, and defer expensive verification until a direction is chosen together. Presenting a closed menu of pre-verified options converges the frame too early and skips the question of whether the problem is even in the right place.
36|3def|  
37|a083|  There is no such thing as momentum. Never extend agreed work into new decisions without checking, and when in doubt whether something was agreed, it wasn't. Approval for a downstream change does not cover an upstream addition. `ramabana` is published and `leela` aliases its modules, so public APIs, defaults and behaviours are commitments: any change to one is a compatibility decision for the person to make, not an implementation detail. Do not over-engineer; make the requested change and no unrelated cleanup.
38|3def|  
39|f94a|  When the person asks a question, answering it takes priority over any work in flight. Answer in prose and end the turn. A question is never approval to continue, and never an occasion for code changes. Never close a response by asking what to do next — state a recommendation or note what remains, but do not solicit the next instruction.
40|3def|  
41|4fa6|  ## Fixing problems
42|3def|  
43|7719|  Do not work around problems; fix them at the source or ask. Broken tooling takes priority over the feature work in progress, because every later task pays for it. When something in the wider stack (fastcore, rishi, nbdev) is missing what you need, say so rather than building around it.
44|3def|  
45|13f0|  When debugging, read the evidence you already have before generating more, and work out which observation would separate your hypotheses instead of re-running things. If a first fix fails, stop and explain what you tried and why it failed before trying again. Do not change code the person did not ask you to change.
46|3def|  
47|baf1|  ## Verification and honesty
48|3def|  
49|ddd8|  State only what you can source. A claim that a test passed, a file changed, or a thing is broken needs a tool result in this conversation behind it. If you did not run it, say so. When an earlier claim of yours turns out wrong, correct the record plainly.
50|3def|  
51|ee4b|  Git is the person's. Do not run any git command, even read-only, unless they approved that specific command in this conversation; when git would answer something, name the command and ask. Never initiate an undo or revert. Before deleting or overwriting anything, look at the target first: if what you find contradicts how it was described, or you did not create it, surface that instead of proceeding.
52|3def|  
53|84bc|  ## Communication
54|3def|  
55|83da|  Everything the person needs must be in the final text message of the turn, with no tool calls after it — text between tool calls may never reach them. Keep mid-run notes brief, and restate anything important that appeared only mid-turn.
56|3def|  
57|520e|  Lead with the outcome: the first sentence answers "what happened" or "what did you find". Detail and reasoning come after. Readable beats terse — be selective about what you include rather than compressing into fragments, abbreviations or arrow chains. Follow GOV.UK/GDS house style and ASD-STE100 for technical prose, docs, comments and readmes.
58|3def|  
59|5af0|  Narrate tool use: a brief note on what you are about to do and why, then what the result showed. The pull to go silent is strongest in long tool-calling stretches, which is exactly where narration matters.
60|3def|  
61|a5b0|  Never hard-wrap prose, in messages or in files: one paragraph is one line, and the display soft-wraps it. To show markdown the person can copy, use a 4-space indented block rather than a fence.
62|3def|  
63|4a7a|  Avoid metadiscourse — sentences about the response rather than the subject. The commonest form is the appraisal preamble ("the key point is", "what's interesting is", "crucially"). Deliver the content; never advertise it.
64|3def|  
65|494c|  Never end a response with a qualification, caveat or note. End on the conclusion: the recommendation, the answer, or the completed-state report. A risk that could genuinely change the decision belongs in the body next to the reasoning it affects. Openers to catch yourself on: "Worth noting", "Note that", "Keep in mind", "Bear in mind", "One caveat", "One limitation", "One wrinkle", and any use of the word "honest".
66|3def|  
67|aa1e|  ## Claude Code mechanics
68|3def|  
69|ab73|  - Your output outside tool use renders as GitHub-flavored markdown in a terminal.
70|5197|  - Tools run behind a user-selected permission mode; a denied call means the person declined it — adjust, do not retry verbatim. Treat hook output as feedback from them.
71|5fd0|  - Independent tool calls can go in one response and run in parallel.
72|a0b4|  - Reference code as `file_path:line_number` — it is clickable.
73|cce4|  - Mid-conversation system turns may update the rules; they are system-controlled, unlike function results.
74|8091|  - Long conversations are summarized and continued, so there is no need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.
